topic_title: Top 7 Fluffiest Dog Breeds That Look Like Teddy Bears
intro: A teddy bear coat is a commitment before it is a look. The fluffiest breeds have long or double coats that mat if they are skipped for a week, and several shed heavily twice a year. Before choosing, decide how many minutes of brushing you can give each week and if you will pay a groomer every six to eight weeks. Size matters too: a large fluffy dog brings a large amount of hair into the house, while the small breeds here shed less but still need daily combing.

picks.description: The Samoyed sets the standard for fluff: a dense white undercoat under long, straight guard hairs that make the whole dog look inflated. That coat comes with work. Expect to brush three or four times a week with a slicker brush and an undercoat rake, and daily when it blows its coat, which leaves drifts of white hair on floors and clothes. Samoyeds are large, friendly and playful, get along with children, cats and other dogs, and train easily, but they need around an hour of exercise a day or they find their own projects. They bark at a medium level and like to be with their people, so long days alone do not suit them. Life expectancy is about 12 to 14 years.
picks.best_for: Active families who enjoy grooming and want a big, sociable fluffy dog
picks.quirky_fact: The upturned corners of the Samoyed's mouth help stop drool from freezing on its face, which is the origin of the so-called Sammy smile.
picks.skip_if: You dislike dog hair on everything or cannot brush several times weekly

picks.description: The Old English Sheepdog is the shaggiest dog on this list, with a long, thick coat that falls over its eyes and gives it a walking-rug outline. Keeping that coat full takes several hours of line brushing each week, down to the skin, or it mats behind the ears and legs. Many owners choose a shorter puppy clip from a groomer to make care manageable. The breed is large, gentle, affectionate and playful, and the data rates it good with children, cats and other dogs. Energy is medium, so a daily walk plus play time is enough for most adults. Training is moderate: they are clever but can be clownish and slow to obey. Shedding is high, and the beard needs wiping after meals and drinks.
picks.best_for: Patient owners with space who want a gentle, shaggy family dog
picks.quirky_fact: Owners in England traditionally docked the tails of drovers' dogs, which is where the breed's old nickname bobtail comes from.
picks.skip_if: You want a tidy dog or cannot pay for regular professional grooming

picks.description: The Tibetan Terrier gives you a full, long double coat in a medium-sized body, which makes it the most manageable large-looking fluff on the list. The coat parts down the back and can be kept long or trimmed short; long coats need brushing every two or three days with a pin brush and comb. Shedding is rated medium, lower than the Samoyed or Old English Sheepdog. Despite the name it is not a true terrier, and it is affectionate, playful and alert rather than scrappy. It gets along with children, cats and other dogs. Expect 45 minutes or so of walks and games a day. Training is moderate, so short, upbeat sessions work better than repetition. Lifespan is long, around 12 to 15 years.
picks.best_for: Owners who want a big fluffy look without a large dog
picks.quirky_fact: Its broad, flat feet act like snowshoes, a trait the breed is thought to have developed in the Himalayan mountains.
picks.skip_if: You want a low-grooming dog or prefer a quick, obedient learner

picks.description: The Lhasa Apso has a floor-length straight coat in show trim, and even a pet trim leaves a plush, rounded look. Kept long, the coat needs daily brushing to the skin; most owners switch to a shorter cut every six to eight weeks. Shedding is rated medium. This is a small, low-energy breed that is content with two short walks and some indoor play, which suits apartments. The trade-off is temperament: Lhasas are independent, alert and stubborn, and the data rates them hard to train, so housebreaking and recall take consistent work. They are loyal and affectionate with their own family but can be reserved with strangers and will bark at unfamiliar sounds. The data rates them good with children, cats and dogs, though they dislike rough handling.
picks.best_for: Calm adults wanting a small, loyal, low-exercise fluffy dog
picks.quirky_fact: Lhasa Apsos were kept as indoor sentinels in Tibetan monasteries, which explains how quickly they announce visitors.
picks.skip_if: You want an eager-to-please dog or are a first-time trainer

picks.description: The Pomeranian packs the most fluff per pound: a toy dog wrapped in a stand-off double coat that makes it look twice its size. That coat sheds heavily and needs brushing two or three times a week, more during seasonal sheds. Pomeranians are friendly, playful and intelligent, with medium energy that is easy to meet with short walks and indoor games. They suit apartments for size, but they are rated high for barking, so expect to teach a quiet cue early, especially in shared buildings. Training is moderate; they learn quickly but can be stubborn. The data rates them good with children, cats and other dogs, though a toy dog can be hurt by rough play or a jump from furniture, so very young children need supervision.
picks.best_for: Adults wanting a tiny, lively dog with a huge fluffy coat
picks.quirky_fact: Early Pomeranians were much larger sled-type dogs; breeders shrank them sharply in the 1800s after Queen Victoria popularized small ones.
picks.skip_if: Barking would bother neighbors or you have toddlers who handle pets roughly

picks.description: The Havanese has a long, silky coat that feels soft rather than dense, and it is rated low for shedding, which makes it one of the easier fluffy dogs to keep in a tidy home. The catch is that loose hair stays in the coat, so it needs daily brushing if kept long, or a short teddy bear trim every six to eight weeks. This small breed is affectionate, friendly, gentle and playful, trains easily, and gets along with children, cats and other dogs. Medium energy means 30 to 45 minutes of walks and play a day is enough. Havanese are very people-focused, so they cope poorly with long hours alone. Barking is medium. With a lifespan of around 14 to 16 years, it is a long commitment.
picks.best_for: Families and first-time owners wanting a soft, low-shedding companion
picks.quirky_fact: The Havanese is the national dog of Cuba, and some owners keep the coat corded like small ropes instead of brushed.
picks.skip_if: You are away all day or will not brush or book regular trims

picks.description: The Shih Tzu has a long, silky double coat that, trimmed short into a puppy cut, gives the round teddy bear face many people are looking for. Shedding is rated low, but a long coat tangles quickly and needs daily brushing, and the hair above the nose is usually tied up or trimmed so it does not irritate the eyes. This is a small, low-energy, calm breed: a couple of short walks and some play indoors keep it content, which suits apartments and older owners. Shih Tzus are affectionate and friendly and the data rates them good with children, cats and dogs. Training is moderate because they can be stubborn, especially with housebreaking. Their short muzzle means they overheat easily, so keep walks short in hot weather.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers and seniors wanting a calm, cuddly small dog
picks.quirky_fact: The name Shih Tzu translates roughly as lion dog, a nod to the lion figures in Chinese Buddhist art.
picks.skip_if: You live somewhere hot without air conditioning or want a jogging partner

faqs.question: What is the fluffiest dog breed?
faqs.answer: The Samoyed has one of the fullest coats of any breed: a dense, white double coat that stands away from the body. The Old English Sheepdog is a close second with a long, shaggy coat that covers its eyes. Both are large dogs that shed heavily and need brushing several times a week, so they suit owners who enjoy grooming.

faqs.question: Which fluffy dogs shed the least?
faqs.answer: In this list, the Havanese and Shih Tzu are rated low for shedding. Their long, silky coats hold loose hair instead of dropping it, which is why they need daily brushing to stop mats forming. No breed is free of allergens, so anyone with dog allergies should spend time with the breed before committing.

faqs.question: How often do fluffy dogs need grooming?
faqs.answer: Plan on brushing large double-coated breeds such as the Samoyed three or four times a week, and daily during seasonal sheds. Long silky coats like the Shih Tzu and Havanese need daily combing if kept long. Many owners book a professional groom every six to eight weeks and ask for a shorter trim to cut daily work.

faqs.question: Are fluffy dogs good in hot weather?
faqs.answer: Thick double coats insulate against heat as well as cold, but heavy-coated breeds still tire quickly in summer. Walk them early or late, offer shade and water, and keep the house cool. Do not shave a double-coated breed such as the Samoyed or Pomeranian, because the coat may grow back unevenly and no longer protect the skin.

faqs.question: Which small fluffy dog is easiest to live with?
faqs.answer: The Havanese is the easiest small fluffy breed here: it trains easily, sheds little and gets along with children, cats and other dogs. The Shih Tzu is similar and calmer. The Pomeranian is fluffier but barks more, and the Lhasa Apso is harder to train, so both suit owners with more patience.

seo_title: Fluffiest Dog Breeds: 7 Teddy Bear Dogs (2026)
answer: The Samoyed, Old English Sheepdog and Tibetan Terrier are the fluffiest breeds here, each with a long, thick double coat. The deciding factor is grooming time: every dog on this list needs regular brushing, and the biggest coats need the most.
method: We filtered a 150-breed dataset for breeds with long, dense or double coats and a high grooming rating, then ordered them by coat volume and size, putting the thickest, fullest coats first.
